edges.description: Loss of glomerular filtration follows the primary proximal tubular lesion in some subtypes rather than all of them: the kindreds in which FRTS1 (GATM) was defined were ascertained through dominant renal Fanconi syndrome with kidney failure, and the FRTS5 (NDUFAF6) form is reported with slowly progressive chronic kidney disease, while FRTS3 (EHHADH) characteristically preserves glomerular filtration. The per-subtype distribution is recorded on the Chronic kidney disease phenotype. The edge runs from the primary lesion rather than from the downstream skeletal consequences.

edges.description: Generalized failure of proximal reabsorption is what the clinical term renal Fanconi syndrome names.
Loss of proximal glucose reabsorption produces glycosuria at normal serum glucose concentrations.
Loss of proximal amino acid reabsorption produces generalized aminoaciduria.
Failure of proximal endocytic reclamation of filtered low-molecular-weight proteins produces tubular proteinuria.
Loss of proximal phosphate reabsorption produces renal phosphate wasting.
Sustained urinary phosphate loss lowers the serum phosphate concentration.
Proximal bicarbonate wasting exceeds the limited distal reclamation capacity, producing a normal anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
Loss of proximal urate reabsorption lowers the serum urate concentration.
Chronic hypophosphatemia from renal phosphate wasting impairs skeletal mineralization, producing rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

nodes.description: Each monogenic FRTS subtype introduces a distinct primary lesion in the proximal tubular epithelial cell: a transcriptional program defect (HNF4A), loss of a specific apical transporter (SLC34A1/NaPi-IIa), or a defect in mitochondrial energy provision (EHHADH mistargeting, NDUFAF6 complex I deficiency, GATM mitochondrial aggregates). Because vectorial proximal reabsorption is highly ATP-dependent, mitochondrial energy failure is a recurrent upstream theme across subtypes.
